tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

/-!
# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.5": the HandlePool
v0.4 annex (items D.1–D.4) as amended by the arbitrations Q3, Q4, Q5 and Q12 (items HP5-1 to
HP5-7). `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` does not define it (Part XIV preamble: "The
contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined
here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the
administering value; `writeShared` alone is insufficient; the library adds no rights to the
kernel), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities; a stale identity or generation leads to
defined failure), §38 and §46 (library state outside `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the
guard over all registries of live administrations), §58 (outcomes) and §76 (the obligations of
`newArena` that `newPool` takes over).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3);
`freeSlot` updates the registry only (HP5-1). Every library step is thus, on the kernel side, a
finite sequence of accepted kernel steps (`pstep_kernel`), so, under `DDSound` (§80) and
`StaticsOK` (§47), every kernel state of a library run is kernel-reachable and satisfies the
invariant of §57 (`kernel_guarantee`, HP5-7).
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.HandlePool

open Ern.MemoryModel
open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Library state (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §38, §46) -/

/-- Slot of a pool entry (HandlePool v0.5, D.1: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`; non-normative
library contract; §38, §46). -/
structure Slot where
  place : Nat
  gen : Nat
  live : Bool
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Pool entry `{storage, internal, slots}` with its logical identity (HandlePool v0.5, D.1;
non-normative library contract). The pool value is the place holding `internal` (§46 analogue). -/
structure Pool where
  id : Nat
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  slots : List Slot
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Handle `(poolId, slot, gen)`: data, not an authority (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §37, §89;
non-normative library contract). -/
structure Handle where
  id : Nat
  slot : Nat
  gen : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Ghost record of a resolution (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; auxiliary information creating no right,
§38): pool identity and `internal`, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities tagged with
their slot and resolved generation. Read by `unresolve`, by the content condition of `freeSlot`
(the companions of a pool, HP5-1) and by the invariants. -/
structure Res where
  pool : Nat
  internal : Nat
  comp : Nat
  mode : Mode
  entries : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Library state (§38, §46; HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library contract): the kernel
state `S₃` and, separately, the pool registry, the next fresh pool identity and the ghost
resolutions. -/
structure PState where
  kern : S3
  pools : List Pool
  nId : Nat

def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
  | s, [] => some s
  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none

/-- The resolution of companion `c` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; ghost lookup, §38). -/
def findRes (L : PState) (c : Nat) : Option Res := L.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c

/-- Authorities released by `unresolve` of `r` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; non-normative library
contract): the entry authorities still active, then the companion (§62). -/
def unresolveList (s : S3) (r : Res) : List Nat :=
  ((r.entries.map (·.1)).filter fun a => decide (s.Active a)) ++ [r.comp]

/-- `unresolve(c)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §58; non-normative library contract): the
releases of `unresolveList`; `reject` when one is not accepted or `c` is no companion. -/
inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | none : findRes L c = none → UnresolveStep c L .reject
  | reject {r : Res} : findRes L c = some r → releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = none →
      UnresolveStep c L .reject
  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes L c = some r →
      releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = some s' →
      UnresolveStep c L (.ok { L with kern := s' })

/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 as amended by HP5-1) -/

/-- No active strict descendant of a companion recorded for pool `pl` covers a leaf of place `q`
(HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1, and D.4 (3) restricted to the companions of the slot's pool, HP5-4; §42:
descendants along the origin chain; non-normative library contract). The companions of `pl` are
those of the resolutions recorded for its identity. -/
def NoCompDesc (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x ∈ List.range L.kern.A.length, L.kern.Active x →
    r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x → ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P q

/-- Decidability of `NoCompDesc` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; §42). -/
instance (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (NoCompDesc L pl q) := by
  unfold NoCompDesc; infer_instance

/-- Content conditions of `freeSlot` on slot place `q` of pool `pl` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1;
non-normative library contract). -/
structure FreeContentOK (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1: no leaf of the entry is `Init`; each is `Uninit` or `Moved`
  (§41). -/
  notInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q, L.kern.I l ≠ .init
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1: no active authority derived from a companion of this pool (a strict
  descendant of a companion recorded for this pool) covers a leaf of the entry. -/
  noCompDesc : NoCompDesc L pl q

/-- Decidability of `FreeContentOK` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; §41, §42). -/
instance (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (FreeContentOK L pl q) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q, L.kern.I l ≠ .init) ∧ NoCompDesc L pl q)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; non-normative library
contract): the slot becomes free and its generation is incremented; there is no end-of-use effect
and the kernel state is unchanged (§36: the library adds no rights to the kernel). -/
def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
  { L with pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }

/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36, HP5-1; §58;
non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool or without the administration right
(live pool and `MetaRight`); then `fail` for a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then
`reject` unless the content conditions hold (`FreeContentOK`). This is the outcome order of
HandlePool v0.4, kept by HP5-1: the order of HP5-5 (handle before right) concerns resolution
(§89) only. -/
inductive FreeSlotStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
      FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl → ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      FreeSlotStep j h L .fail
  | noContent {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK L.kern pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ FreeContentOK L pl sl.place →
      FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK L.kern pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → FreeContentOK L pl sl.place →
      FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))

/-! ## Library runs (HandlePool v0.5; §38, §46, §47) -/

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.5; non-normative library contract): a kernel
step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool operation
(§58). -/
......
theorem pReach_compExcl {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hdd : DDSound k) (hst : StaticsOK statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : CompExcl L := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro r hr; simp [PState.init] at hr
  | step hr hs ih =>
    exact pstep_compExcl (kernel_guarantee hdd hst _ hr).2.1.1.1 (pReach_poolWF hr) ih hs

/-! ## `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 per pool, HP5-4) -/

/-- `PoolInv`, item 1 (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 (1); non-normative library contract): the entries of
every pool lie in its storage and are pairwise disjoint (§40). -/
def EntriesDisjoint (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ pl ∈ L.pools,
    (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sl.place, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) ∧
    ∀ (a b : Nat) (sa sb : Slot), pl.slots[a]? = some sa → pl.slots[b]? = some sb → a ≠ b →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sa.place, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sb.place

/-- `PoolInv`, item 2, `pool_no_stale_access` as a state predicate (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 (2);
non-normative library contract): no active entry authority designates a free slot or a former
generation (§89). -/
def NoStale (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ e ∈ r.entries, L.kern.Active e.1 → ∃ pl ∈ L.pools, pl.id = r.pool ∧
    ∃ sl, pl.slots[e.2.1]? = some sl ∧ sl.gen = e.2.2 ∧ sl.live = true

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee per pool (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 (3) restricted to

d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné"; non-normative library contract): `freeSlot` never
succeeds while an active strict descendant of a companion of the slot's pool covers a leaf of the
slot (§42, §43). -/

state, `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active strict descendant of a companion of the slot's

the pool, HP5-4: "La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du
noyau"): on every library-reachable state, under `DDSound` (§80) and `StaticsOK` (§47), whatever

theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := pReach_compExcl hdd hst h r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1

theorem not_handleOK_dead {s : S3} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} (hd : ¬ s.Active pl.internal) :
    ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨ha, _⟩ => hd ha

/-- A handle of another pool is not valid (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, D.3; §89). -/

    ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨_, e, _⟩ => hid e

/-- A stale handle is not valid (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, D.3; §89). -/

  fun ⟨_, _, ho⟩ => by rw [hsl] at ho; exact hg ho.1

/-! # Counterexample to `pool_no_stale_access` (and `pool_inv_preserved`) under HandlePool v0.5

Scratch file: a copy of `formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean` followed by this section. Run from
`formal/` with `~/.elan/bin/lake env lean <this file>`.

pool value (`Init`); place 4 is the handle destination; place 5 is a leaf of frame 0 that will hold
the entry authority. Root authorities 0, 1, 2, 3 cover places 0, 3, 4, 5. No client kernel step
has a companion as source or argument: the companion is created by `resolve` in frame 1, held by
frame 1, and dies when frame 1 exits (§73). The entry authority, stored in place 5 of frame 0,
survives and is reanchored to `internal` (§73.4), so it is no longer a descendant of the
companion, and HP5-1's content condition no longer sees it. -/

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.Lib.HandlePool Examples

def cst : Statics :=

/-- `store(4, 3)`: `internal` held by the pool value 3. -/
def c2 : PState := { c1 with kern := storeEff c1.kern 4 3 }
/-- `newPool(0, 4)`. -/
def c3 : PState := newPoolEff c2 0 4
def pA : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 0, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩
/-- `allocSlot(0, 4)`: handle ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ written into place 4. -/

def pA4 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 0, true⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩
/-- `derive(1, [3], Modify)`: authority 5 over the pool value. -/
def c5 : PState := { c4 with kern := deriveEff c4.kern 1 [3] .modify }
/-- `derive(3, [5], Modify)`: authority 6 over place 5. -/
def c6 : PState := { c5 with kern := deriveEff c5.kern 3 [5] .modify }
/-- `enterFrame([5, 6], [])`: frame 1. -/
def c7 : PState := { c6 with kern := enterEff c6.kern [5, 6] [] }
/-- `resolve(0, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` in frame 1: companion 7, entry authority 8 over slot place 1. -/

/-- `store(8, 5)`: the entry authority is stored into place 5 of frame 0. -/

(§65). The local is place 5, created by `enterFrame` (§72) and owned by the current frame 1. The
transfer is accepted through the exemption of v0.1 §63.4: the entry authority 7, which grounds the
right over the source, its companion 6, `internal` 3 and its origin 0 cover the source from

    x7.kern.P[5]? = some ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩ ∧ x7.kern.top = 1 ∧

    x7.pools[0]? = some ⟨0, 0, 3, [⟨1, 1, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩ := by
  have r3 : ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify x2 (.ok x3) :=

library contract): entry disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of
`freeSlot` (§55, §57). It is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- Same-pool restriction of `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): items 1 and 2 as the contract states them, item 3 restricted to the companions of the
slot's pool (`FreeGuaranteeSamePool`). This is not the contract's statement (`PoolInv`) (§55,
§57). -/
def PoolInvSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The same-pool transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3, restricted to the slot's pool): an active descendant of a
companion of the pool is younger than `internal`, so it is neither `internal` nor one of its
ancestors, and `ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43, §69). -/
theorem freeGuaranteeSamePool_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) :
    FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInvSamePool`
holds on every state of a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with
`PReach.toI`, on every library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. This is not the
contract's statement: `PoolInv` is false on such a state (`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : PoolInvSamePool k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3):
on every state of a library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while the companion of a

    {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape}
    {pl : Placement} {g : Nat → Geom} (hdd : DDSound k) (hst : StaticsOK statics)
    (hr : Access.Reachable k statics s3) (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2)
    (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s3 (.ok s3')) (hpl : PlacementOK pl) (hg : GeomOK g)
    (hlay : NewLayout L (allocP s3 ow ls) s3.P.length s2.next g (rootIdx ls.toShape)) :
    (allocOps (Ty := Ty) pl g rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)).length = 1 ∧
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (allocOps pl g rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)) s2
        (run s2 (allocOps (Ty := Ty) pl g rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape))) ∧
      Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (allocOps (Ty := Ty) pl g rtok s3.P.length s2
        (rootIdx ls.toShape))) :=
  r6_alloc hR (reachable_kinv hdd hst hr).1 h hpl hg hlay

/-- R4 on reachable states (§82.5, §54, §57): under `DDSound` (§80) and `StaticsOK` (§47),
`r4_no_dead_cover` without invariant hypothesis. -/
theorem r4_no_dead_cover_reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat}
    {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} (hdd : DDSound k) (hst : StaticsOK statics)
    (hr : Access.Reachable k statics s3) (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) {j : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hy : s3.A[j]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ y.footprint) :
    l < s3.P.length ∧ isLeaf s3.P l ∧
      AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size :=
  have hk := reachable_kinv hdd hst hr
  r4_no_dead_cover hR hk.1 hk.2.1.2.2 hy ya hl

p='Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean'
s=open(p).read()
anchor="""    by decide, by decide⟩

end Witness
"""
assert s.count(anchor)==1
new='''    by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ### `pool_no_stale_access` after a frame exit (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 (2), HP5-1; §42, §73)

Statics `cst` (§47): place 0 is the pool storage with leaf children 1 and 2 (`Uninit`); place 3 is
the pool value (`Init`); place 4 is the handle destination; place 5 is a leaf of frame 0. Root
authorities 0 to 3 cover places 0, 3, 4 and 5. Frame 1 resolves the handle in `Modify`; the entry
authority is stored into place 5 of frame 0; at the exit of frame 1 the companion dies and the entry
authority is reanchored to `internal` (§73); `freeSlot` is then accepted. -/

/-- Statics of the run (§47; HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
def cst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false),
    ((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false), ((none, none, 0), false)]
/-- After `derive(0, [1, 2], Modify)` (§60): `internal` is authority 4 (HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
def c1 : PState := { PState.init cst with kern := deriveEff (PState.init cst).kern 0 [1, 2] .modify }
/-- After `store(4, 3)` (§65): `internal` is held by the pool value (HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
def c2 : PState := { c1 with kern := storeEff c1.kern 4 3 }
/-- After `newPool(0, 4)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §76). -/
def c3 : PState := newPoolEff c2 0 4
/-- Pool 0 after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §47). -/
def pA : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 0, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩
/-- After `allocSlot(0, 4)`: the handle `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is written into place 4 (HandlePool v0.5, D.3;
§67). -/
def c4 : PState := allocSlotEff c3 0 pA 0 ⟨1, 0, false⟩ 4
/-- Pool 0 after `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; §47). -/
def pA4 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 0, true⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩
/-- After `derive(1, [3], Modify)`: authority 5 over the pool value (§60; HandlePool v0.5). -/
def c5 : PState := { c4 with kern := deriveEff c4.kern 1 [3] .modify }
/-- After `derive(3, [5], Modify)`: authority 6 over place 5 (§60; HandlePool v0.5). -/
def c6 : PState := { c5 with kern := deriveEff c5.kern 3 [5] .modify }
/-- After `enterFrame([5, 6], [])`: frame 1 (§72; HandlePool v0.5). -/
def c7 : PState := { c6 with kern := enterEff c6.kern [5, 6] [] }
/-- After `resolve(0, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` in frame 1: companion 7, entry authority 8 over slot
place 1 (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60). -/
def c8 : PState := { c7 with
  kern := deriveEff (compS c7.kern pA4 .modify) c7.kern.A.length (footprint c7.kern.P 1) .modify
  res := c7.res ++ [⟨pA4.id, pA4.internal, c7.kern.A.length, .modify,
    [(c7.kern.A.length + 1, 0, 0)]⟩] }
/-- After `store(8, 5)`: the entry authority is held by place 5 of frame 0 (§65; HandlePool
v0.5). -/
def c9 : PState := { c8 with kern := storeEff c8.kern 8 5 }
/-- After `exitFrame`: the companion 7 dies with frame 1; the entry authority 8 survives,
reanchored to `internal` 4 (§73; HandlePool v0.5). -/
def c10 : PState := { c9 with kern := exitEff c9.kern }
/-- After `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` in frame 0 (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; §36, §38). -/
def c11 : PState := freeSlotEff c10 0 pA4 0 ⟨1, 0, true⟩

/-- Open point (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 (2), "aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre
ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`)", against the HP5-1 content condition read
along the current origin chain, §42; non-normative library contract). Under `DDSound` (§80) and
`StaticsOK` (§47), `c11` is library-reachable; in `c10` the entry authority 8, recorded for slot 0
at generation 0, is active `Modify` over slot place 1 with origin `internal` 4 (reanchored, §73),
and the companion 7 is inactive, so `freeSlot` is accepted; in `c11` slot 0 is free at generation 1
while 8 is still active: `NoStale` and `PoolInv` are false. -/
theorem no_stale_after_exit :
    DDSound K0 ∧ StaticsOK cst ∧ PReach K0 cst c11 ∧
    (⟨0, 4, 7, .modify, [(8, 0, 0)]⟩ : Res) ∈ c10.res ∧
    c10.kern.A[8]? = some ⟨.modify, some 4, [1], .place 5, true⟩ ∧ ¬ c10.kern.Active 7 ∧
    c11.pools = [⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 1, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩] ∧ c11.kern.Active 8 ∧
    ¬ NoStale c11 ∧ ¬ PoolInv c11 := by
  have h3 : PReach K0 cst c3 :=
    .step (.step (.step .init (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))))
      (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  have h4 : PReach K0 cst c4 := .step h3 (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := pA) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))
  have h7 : PReach K0 cst c7 :=
    .step (.step (.step h4 (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))))
      (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (.kernel (.enter (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have r8 : ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify c7 (.ok c8) :=
    .ok (pl := pA4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have h10 : PReach K0 cst c10 := .step (.step (.step h7 (.resolve r8))
    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (.kernel (.exit (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have f11 : FreeSlotStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ c10 (.ok c11) :=
    .ok (pl := pA4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have hp : c11.pools = [⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 1, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩] := by decide
  have hn : ¬ NoStale c11 := fun h => by
    obtain ⟨pl, hpl, -, sl, hsl, -, hlv⟩ :=
      h ⟨0, 4, 7, .modify, [(8, 0, 0)]⟩ (by decide) (8, 0, 0) (by decide) (by decide)
    rw [hp, List.mem_singleton] at hpl
    subst hpl
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at hsl
    subst hsl
    cases hlv
  exact ⟨fun _ _ h => h.elim, by decide, .step h10 (.freeSlot f11), by decide, by decide,
    by decide, hp, by decide, hn, fun hi => hn hi.2.1⟩

/-! ### The write of HP5-3 on a pool value with a `Moved` leaf (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-3; §63, §67)

Statics `vst` (§47): place 0, the pool value, `Init`, with leaves 1 and 2; place 3, the storage,
owned by place 0, with `Uninit` leaves 4 and 5; place 6, an `Uninit` leaf of frame 0. `internal`
is the root authority 1 of the storage, held by its owner, place 0. -/

/-- Statics of the run (§47; HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
def vst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true),
    ((none, some 0, 0), false), ((some 3, some 0, 0), false), ((some 3, some 0, 0), false),
    ((none, none, 0), false)]
/-- After `newPool(3, 1)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §76). -/
def m1 : PState := newPoolEff (PState.init vst) 3 1
/-- After the kernel `transfer(1, 6)` of leaf 1 of the pool value to place 6 (§63; HandlePool
v0.5). -/
def m2 : PState := { m1 with kern := transferEff m1.kern 1 6 }
/-- Pool 0 after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §47). -/
def pv : Pool := ⟨0, 3, 1, [⟨4, 0, false⟩, ⟨5, 0, false⟩]⟩

/-- Limit of HP5-3 (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-3; non-normative library contract): `m2` is
library-reachable, pool 0 has `AdminRight` (§36) and its value, place 0, has the `Moved` leaf 1
(§63); the write of the leaves of the pool value (§67) that `freeSlot_meta_write` provides is then
not the identity on the kernel state, while `freeSlot` leaves the kernel state unchanged
(`freeSlot_effect`). -/
theorem meta_write_not_identity :
    StaticsOK vst ∧ PReach K0 vst m2 ∧ m2.pools[0]? = some pv ∧ AdminRight m2.kern pv ∧
    Arena.arenaValue m2.kern pv.entry = some 0 ∧ m2.kern.I 1 = .moved ∧
    write3Eff m2.kern (footprint m2.kern.P 0) ≠ m2.kern := by
  have hne : write3Eff m2.kern (footprint m2.kern.P 0) ≠ m2.kern := fun e => by
    have h1 := congrArg (fun s : S3 => s.I 1) e
    have : (write3Eff m2.kern (footprint m2.kern.P 0)).I 1 = .init := by decide
    have h2 : m2.kern.I 1 = .moved := by decide
    rw [this, h2] at h1; cases h1
  exact ⟨by decide, .step (.step .init (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
    (.kernel (.transfer (Guarded.ok (by decide)))), rfl, by decide, by decide, by decide, hne⟩

end Witness
'''
s=s.replace(anchor,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

/-- After `enterFrame([5, 6], [])`: frame 1 (§72; HandlePool v0.5). -/
def c7 : PState := { c6 with kern := enterEff c6.kern [5, 6] [] }
/-- After `resolve(0, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` in frame 1: companion 7, entry authority 8 over slot
place 1 (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60). -/
def c8 : PState := { c7 with
  kern := deriveEff (compS c7.kern pA4 .modify) c7.kern.A.length (footprint c7.kern.P 1) .modify
  res := c7.res ++ [⟨pA4.id, pA4.internal, c7.kern.A.length, .modify,
    [(c7.kern.A.length + 1, 0, 0)]⟩] }
/-- After `store(8, 5)`: the entry authority is held by place 5 of frame 0 (§65; HandlePool
v0.5). -/
def c9 : PState := { c8 with kern := storeEff c8.kern 8 5 }
/-- After `exitFrame`: the companion 7 dies with frame 1; the entry authority 8 survives,
reanchored to `internal` 4 (§73; HandlePool v0.5). -/
def c10 : PState := { c9 with kern := exitEff c9.kern }
/-- After `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` in frame 0 (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; §36, §38). -/
def c11 : PState := freeSlotEff c10 0 pA4 0 ⟨1, 0, true⟩

/-- Open point (HandlePool v0.5, D.4 (2), "aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre
ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`)", against the HP5-1 content condition read
along the current origin chain, §42; non-normative library contract). Under `DDSound` (§80) and
`StaticsOK` (§47), `c11` is library-reachable; in `c10` the entry authority 8, recorded for slot 0
at generation 0, is active `Modify` over slot place 1 with origin `internal` 4 (reanchored, §73),
and the companion 7 is inactive, so `freeSlot` is accepted; in `c11` slot 0 is free at generation 1
while 8 is still active: `NoStale` and `PoolInv` are false. -/
theorem no_stale_after_exit :
    DDSound K0 ∧ StaticsOK cst ∧ PReach K0 cst c11 ∧
    (⟨0, 4, 7, .modify, [(8, 0, 0)]⟩ : Res) ∈ c10.res ∧
    c10.kern.A[8]? = some ⟨.modify, some 4, [1], .place 5, true⟩ ∧ ¬ c10.kern.Active 7 ∧
    c11.pools = [⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 1, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩] ∧ c11.kern.Active 8 ∧
    ¬ NoStale c11 ∧ ¬ PoolInv c11 := by
  have h3 : PReach K0 cst c3 :=
    .step (.step (.step .init (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))))
      (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  have h4 : PReach K0 cst c4 := .step h3 (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := pA) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))
  have h7 : PReach K0 cst c7 :=
    .step (.step (.step h4 (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))))
      (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (.kernel (.enter (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have r8 : ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify c7 (.ok c8) :=
    .ok (pl := pA4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have h10 : PReach K0 cst c10 := .step (.step (.step h7 (.resolve r8))
    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (.kernel (.exit (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have f11 : FreeSlotStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ c10 (.ok c11) :=
    .ok (pl := pA4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have hp : c11.pools = [⟨0, 0, 4, [⟨1, 1, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩] := by decide
  have hn : ¬ NoStale c11 := fun h => by
    obtain ⟨pl, hpl, -, sl, hsl, -, hlv⟩ :=
      h ⟨0, 4, 7, .modify, [(8, 0, 0)]⟩ (by decide) (8, 0, 0) (by decide) (by decide)
    rw [hp, List.mem_singleton] at hpl
    subst hpl
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at hsl
    subst hsl
    cases hlv
  exact ⟨fun _ _ h => h.elim, by decide, .step h10 (.freeSlot f11), by decide, by decide,
    by decide, hp, by decide, hn, fun hi => hn hi.2.1⟩

/-! ### The write of HP5-3 on a pool value with a `Moved` leaf (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-3; §63, §67)

Statics `vst` (§47): place 0, the pool value, `Init`, with leaves 1 and 2; place 3, the storage,
owned by place 0, with `Uninit` leaves 4 and 5; place 6, an `Uninit` leaf of frame 0. `internal`
is the root authority 1 of the storage, held by its owner, place 0. -/

/-- Statics of the run (§47; HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
def vst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true),
    ((none, some 0, 0), false), ((some 3, some 0, 0), false), ((some 3, some 0, 0), false),
    ((none, none, 0), false)]
/-- After `newPool(3, 1)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §76). -/
def m1 : PState := newPoolEff (PState.init vst) 3 1
/-- After the kernel `transfer(1, 6)` of leaf 1 of the pool value to place 6 (§63; HandlePool
v0.5). -/
def m2 : PState := { m1 with kern := transferEff m1.kern 1 6 }
/-- Pool 0 after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §47). -/
def pv : Pool := ⟨0, 3, 1, [⟨4, 0, false⟩, ⟨5, 0, false⟩]⟩

/-- Limit of HP5-3 (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-3; non-normative library contract): `m2` is
library-reachable, pool 0 has `AdminRight` (§36) and its value, place 0, has the `Moved` leaf 1
(§63); the write of the leaves of the pool value (§67) that `freeSlot_meta_write` provides is then
not the identity on the kernel state, while `freeSlot` leaves the kernel state unchanged
(`freeSlot_effect`). -/
theorem meta_write_not_identity :
    StaticsOK vst ∧ PReach K0 vst m2 ∧ m2.pools[0]? = some pv ∧ AdminRight m2.kern pv ∧
    Arena.arenaValue m2.kern pv.entry = some 0 ∧ m2.kern.I 1 = .moved ∧
    write3Eff m2.kern (footprint m2.kern.P 0) ≠ m2.kern := by
  have hne : write3Eff m2.kern (footprint m2.kern.P 0) ≠ m2.kern := fun e => by
    have h1 := congrArg (fun s : S3 => s.I 1) e
    have : (write3Eff m2.kern (footprint m2.kern.P 0)).I 1 = .init := by decide
    have h2 : m2.kern.I 1 = .moved := by decide
    rw [this, h2] at h1; cases h1
  exact ⟨by decide, .step (.step .init (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
    (.kernel (.transfer (Guarded.ok (by decide)))), rfl, by decide, by decide, by decide, hne⟩

end Witness
'''

open(p,'w').write(s)

input.summary:
I checked all 8 findings against v0.1, the briefs, the arbitration and the code. Six are applied in full and one in part (finding 3). Finding 4 was applied as rewording only, because its substance is an arbitration gap. No theorem statement was changed. Nothing is committed.

Findings 1 and 5 (pool_no_stale_access): real. v0.1 §42 says "`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin". §73 reanchors surviving derived authorities to "the first surviving active origin". So the HP5-1 condition `NoCompDesc`, read along the current chain, stops seeing an entry authority once the frame that ran `resolve` has exited. I rebuilt the reviewer's run inside the module as `Witness.no_stale_after_exit`. It proves `DDSound K0 ∧ StaticsOK cst ∧ PReach K0 cst c11`, plus the shape (entry 8 active `Modify` with origin `internal` 4, companion 7 inactive, slot 0 free at generation 1), and `¬ NoStale c11 ∧ ¬ PoolInv c11`. The `NoStale` and `PoolInv` docstrings now say this and name the open reading. `pool_no_stale_access` and `pool_inv_preserved` are false as stated, so they cannot be proved; they are left to the user.

Findings 2 and 6 (HP5-3): real. I added `Witness.meta_write_not_identity`. The `freeSlot_meta_write` docstring no longer suggests that §76.5 secures the identity condition: it says §76.5 constrains creation only, and that on a reachable state with `AdminRight` and a `Moved` leaf the write changes the kernel state while `freeSlot` does not.

Finding 3: partly applied. Docstrings now carry the missing § citations: `FreeContentOK` (§41, §42), `freeSlot_effect` (§36, §58) and `Witness.x7` (§36, §38). The request to add "non-normative" to every docstring is rejected (reason in open).

Finding 4 (DS-R1, DS-R4): real as a gap in the arbitration. The `reading_above` and `reading_grow_zero` docstrings and the Witness section header now call these readings open, not "kept". They state that Q23 says Q11, Q27 and Q28 decide DS-R1 to DS-R13, yet none of their items names DS-R1 or DS-R4. The formal content is unchanged.

Findings 7 and 8: real, citations only. `r6_read_reachable` now cites the obligations along the reads (§20.3), `r6_exit_reachable` cites the token compatibility (§17.2), and `Runs.sim_of` cites `StaticsOK` (§47).

Checks: `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main Ern.MemoryModel.RefinementArena Ern.Lib.HandlePool Ern.Lib.DataStack` succeeds with no warnings. axcheck on Arena, Refinement, RefinementArena, HandlePool and DataStack reports no axiom outside propext and Quot.sound. `#print axioms` of both new witnesses gives [propext, Quot.sound]. The forbidden-token grep is empty. No kernel change is needed.
